cases.expected: Message.isSigned() returns false; Message.getTSIG() returns null; internal tsigState equals Message.TSIG_UNSIGNED (0)
cases.description: Calling setTSIG(null) should clear any existing TSIG information and leave the message unsigned.

cases.expected: No exception is thrown; method returns normally.
cases.description: Verify that passing a null TSIG does not cause a NullPointerException or any other runtime exception.

cases.expected: Message.isSigned() returns true; Message.getTSIG() returns a TSIGRecord whose key name matches the supplied TSIG; internal tsigState equals Message.TSIG_SIGNED (3)
cases.description: When a non‑null TSIG key is supplied, the message should be marked as signed and a TSIGRecord should be generated.

cases.expected: Message.isSigned() returns true; Message.getTSIG() is not null; tsigState == Message.TSIG_SIGNED (3)
cases.description: Edge case: TSIG with an empty secret should still cause the message to be marked as signed (the library does not validate secret length at setTSIG time).

cases.expected: After first call, isSigned() == true and tsigState == TSIG_SIGNED; after second call with a different key, isSigned() == true and tsigState == TSIG_SIGNED and the TSIGRecord reflects the second key.
cases.description: Calling setTSIG twice should replace the previous TSIG information with the new one, without leaving the message in an intermediate or failed state.

cases.expected: After a previous signed TSIG, calling setTSIG(null) clears the TSIG; isSigned() == false and tsigState == TSIG_UNSIGNED (0).
cases.description: Ensure that a subsequent call with a null key resets the message to an unsigned state.

input.value: mock(TSIG.class) that throws IOException when used

cases.expected: Method does not propagate the IOException; it either logs the error and leaves the message unsigned (tsigState == TSIG_FAILED (4)) or throws a RuntimeException as defined by the library. The test asserts that no checked exception leaks.
cases.description: Simulate a TSIG implementation that fails during internal processing to verify that setTSIG handles the failure gracefully.

cases.expected: Message.isSigned() returns true; Message.getTSIG() returns a TSIGRecord whose name is the Unicode name ("ñame.example.") and algorithm is "hmac-sha256"; internal tsigState equals Message.TSIG_SIGNED (3); no exception is thrown.
cases.description: Verify that a TSIG whose key name contains non‑ASCII characters is accepted and correctly stored in the generated TSIGRecord.

cases.expected: Message.isSigned() returns true; Message.getTSIG() is not null and contains a secret of length 5000; tsigState == Message.TSIG_SIGNED (3); Message.numBytes() <= Message.MAXLENGTH (65535) – the library should truncate or handle the large secret without throwing.
cases.description: Stress‑test the handling of a TSIG with an unusually large secret to ensure the method does not overflow buffers or throw unexpected exceptions.

cases.expected: Message.isSigned() returns false; Message.getTSIG() returns null; tsigState == Message.TSIG_FAILED (4); no checked exception propagates from setTSIG.
cases.description: A TSIG with a null algorithm is invalid; the method should fail gracefully, marking the message as TSIG_FAILED without throwing a checked exception.

cases.expected: After setTSIG, Message.getHeader().getID() is unchanged from its value before the call; Message.isSigned() == true; tsigState == Message.TSIG_SIGNED (3).
cases.description: Ensure that adding a TSIG does not modify unrelated header fields such as the message ID.

cases.expected: After first call, Message.isSigned() == true and Message.getTSIG().getName() == "first.example."; after a second call with a different key (see second case), the original TSIGRecord is removed from the additional section and replaced by the new one; tsigState remains Message.TSIG_SIGNED (3).
cases.description: First call establishes a TSIG; a subsequent call with a new TSIG should replace the existing TSIGRecord rather than appending another.

cases.expected: Message.isSigned() == true; Message.getTSIG().getName() == "second.example."; the additional section contains exactly one TSIGRecord whose key matches the second TSIG; tsigState == Message.TSIG_SIGNED (3).
cases.description: Second call replaces the first TSIG; verify that only one TSIGRecord exists after replacement.

cases.expected: All non‑TSIG sections (ANSWER, AUTHORITY, ADDITIONAL except the generated TSIG) retain the same Record objects and order as before the call; only the TSIGRecord is added/updated in the ADDITIONAL section; Message.getSection(Message.ADDITIONAL).size() increases by 1 if no TSIG was present before, otherwise stays the same.
cases.description: Confirm that setTSIG does not inadvertently modify or reorder records in sections other than the TSIG record itself.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException is thrown (or Message.tsigState becomes TSIG_FAILED) because the TSIG key name is null.
cases.description: A TSIG with a null Name should be rejected by setTSIG, resulting in an IllegalArgumentException (the library validates that the key name is non‑null).

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException is thrown (or tsigState == TSIG_FAILED) because the TSIG key name is not absolute (does not end with a trailing dot).
cases.description: The DNS specification requires TSIG key names to be fully qualified. Passing a relative name must cause setTSIG to reject the key.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException is thrown (or tsigState == TSIG_FAILED) because the key name exceeds the 255‑octet DNS name limit.
cases.description: Create a TSIG whose name label length is 256 characters, exceeding the DNS maximum. setTSIG should detect this and throw an IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException is thrown (or tsigState == TSIG_FAILED) because the secret byte array is null.
cases.description: A TSIG with a null secret is invalid; setTSIG must guard against a NullPointerException and instead raise an IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException is thrown (or tsigState == TSIG_FAILED) because the algorithm string is not one of the supported HMAC algorithms.
cases.description: The library only supports a predefined set of HMAC algorithms. Supplying an unknown algorithm name should cause setTSIG to reject the key with an IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: Message.tsigState becomes TSIG_FAILED (4) and Message.isSigned() returns false; no exception propagates from setTSIG itself.
cases.description: A secret larger than the maximum DNS message size should not cause setTSIG to throw, but the internal state must be marked as failed because the resulting message would exceed MAXLENGTH.
